identity: Maastricht University, full-time Dutch-language Rechtsgeleerdheid LLB, 2026–2027 entrants

sources.scope: English overview confirms Dutch-language, full-time three-year LLB in Maastricht.
Dutch overview independently confirms identity and the three-year duration.
Why this programme confirms main legal fields, a sequence of introductory and deeper courses, problems in society, small-group legal skills and the internship option.

The public structure confirms three 60 EC years. Its detailed block table is explicitly provisional for 2027–2028. Its 24 EC elective and 9 EC thesis figures are not applicable to the 2026–2027 entrant comparison.

2026–2027 EER, adopted 24 March 2026, Article 1 identifies the applicable entrants. Articles 6–10 establish identity, load and structure. Articles 11–14 govern choice, thesis, completion and problem-based instruction. Article 18 explains MaRBLe, Article 22 progression, Articles 36–37 study advice, and Appendix 5 the legal and interdisciplinary competencies.
Graduate destinations and later master’s options, used for search context. The current page names banks without detailing a specific company advisory role.

curriculum: For 2026–2027 entrants, Article 10 gives Year 1 as 27 + 27 + 6 EC including professional skills. Year 2 is 27 + 27 + 6 EC including professional skills. Semester 5 is 27 EC of courses plus 3 EC of thesis methods. Semester 6 is 3 EC professional skills, 12 EC of open choices and 15 EC of thesis. The 27 unique components total 180 EC. There is no required named track. Article 11 permits a legal internship, courses at other faculties, law courses, an approved individual project up to 6 EC or MaRBLe. MaRBLe can use the 12 EC space, with 6 EC extracurricular. The research proposal and thesis form one 18 EC component under Article 12. The proposed 2027–2028 public schedule has different components and credit allocations.
progression: Article 22 requires two of introductory administrative, constitutional and international/European law for Semester 3, introductory private law for Semester 4, and introductory foundations, criminal law and procedure, private law and administrative law for Semester 5. Article 12 requires a passed research proposal before thesis writing. The standard 60 EC first-year plan covers the 40 EC negative-advice threshold in Articles 36–37. All required components must pass for the bachelor exam under Article 13. Appendix 5 progresses from simple legal cases to complex multidisciplinary problems and from basic source-finding to selecting and evaluating legislation, case law and literature.
